AGENTS.md — Project-Level Agent Rules for irishbuoys

Mandatory Workflow Rules

NEVER Skip or Rationalize Away Workflow Steps

The 9-step workflow has NO optional steps. Every step MUST be executed.

Anti-pattern (from fix #30): Marking Step 5 (cachix push) as “N/A” with a rationalization that “it’s not needed for this change”. The user caught it. The correct behavior: if a step is blocked, solve the blocker, don’t declare the step unnecessary.

Rule: If ANY of the 9 steps cannot be executed: 1. Identify the specific blocker (e.g., “cachix binary not on PATH”) 2. Solve the blocker (e.g., nix-shell -p cachix --run '...') 3. Execute the step 4. NEVER mark a step as “N/A”, “skipped”, or “not needed”

Solve Blockers Instead of Declaring Steps Impossible

When a CLI tool isn’t on PATH in the current shell:

# WRONG: "cachix not found, skipping cachix push"
./push_to_cachix.sh  # fails -> give up

# RIGHT: Use nix-shell -p to get the tool
nix-shell -p cachix --run "./push_to_cachix.sh"

# Other examples:
nix-shell -p git-lfs --run "git lfs pull"
nix-shell -p quarto --run "quarto render vignette.qmd"

Pattern: nix-shell -p <tool> --run "<command>" solves most “command not found” issues instantly. Don’t waste time investigating alternatives or giving up.

Understand Architecture Before Dismissing Work

Anti-pattern (from fix #30): Assumed cachix push was critical for CI, then when asked, had to investigate to discover CI loads irishbuoys from source (devtools::load_all()), not from cachix.

Rule: Before claiming a step is or isn’t needed, understand HOW the system works: - CI workflows use nix-shell default.nix for dependencies only - irishbuoys itself is loaded from source via devtools::load_all() - package.nix builds the installable derivation for downstream consumers - push_to_cachix.sh publishes to johngavin cache for other projects/users

Parallel Agent Execution

Always Parallelize Independent Steps

Anti-pattern: Running document, test, check, tar_make, and QA sequentially.

Rule: At Step 4, launch these agents in parallel immediately:

# Three parallel agents (sonnet model each):
1. r-debugger    -> devtools::document() + test() + check()
2. targets-runner -> targets::tar_make()
3. reviewer      -> adversarial QA / quality gate

Don’t wait to be asked. The 9-step workflow CLAUDE.md already says to parallelize – do it from the start.

CI Architecture Notes (irishbuoys-specific)

Nix Caching Strategy (Four-Tier Waterfall)

CI resolves Nix store paths in this priority order:

# 1. DeterminateSystems magic cache (free, automatic, CI-only)
- uses: DeterminateSystems/magic-nix-cache-action@main

# 2-3. Cachix caches (johngavin for all deps + rstats-on-nix for common pkgs)
- uses: cachix/cachix-action@v15
  with:
    name: rstats-on-nix
    extraPullNames: johngavin

# 4. cache.nixos.org (system libs), then compile from source
Cache Purpose Coverage Eviction
magic-nix-cache GH Actions cache for CI All paths from previous runs 7 days without access
johngavin Full dev shell + package ALL 51 R deps (after seeding) Manual/GC
rstats-on-nix Curated popular R packages ~20 of 51 deps (~60 total pkgs) Weekly rebuild
cache.nixos.org System libraries glibc, gcc, etc. nixpkgs releases

Key insight: rstats-on-nix caches only ~60 curated packages, NOT all of CRAN. ~31 of irishbuoys’ 51 deps (targets, DT, plotly, crew, etc.) are NOT on rstats-on-nix and WILL compile from source unless johngavin cachix is seeded.

Cachix Push Scripts (Two Distinct Purposes)

Script Pushes When to Run Guards
push_to_cachix.sh ONLY package.nix (1 derivation) Every release (Step 5) Strict: aborts if >1 R pkg path pushed
seed_dev_cache.sh Full default.nix -A shell (all deps) After default.R/default.nix changes None — intentionally pushes everything
seed-cachix.yml Both dev shell + package Weekly (Monday 3am UTC) Requires CACHIX_AUTH_TOKEN secret

NEVER confuse these: push_to_cachix.sh has strict guards to prevent accidentally filling johngavin cachix with common packages. seed_dev_cache.sh intentionally pushes all deps — that’s the whole point.

Pipeline State: targets-runs Branch Pattern

Pipeline state (_targets/) is stored on a separate orphan branch called targets-runs, NOT on main. This keeps main clean of binary pipeline artifacts.

How it works (weekly-update.yml): 1. Checkout main (source code) 2. Restore _targets/ from targets-runs branch (incremental state) 3. Run tar_make() (only rebuilds changed targets) 4. Render vignettes (tar_load() works – _targets/ is present) 5. Commit rendered outputs (inst/extdata/*.rds, docs/) to main 6. Save _targets/ state to targets-runs branch for next run

Key files: - .targets-files — manifest of pipeline output files (on targets-runs) - _targets/ — gitignored on main, committed on targets-runs - inst/extdata/*.rds — on main (LFS for large files)

How irishbuoys is Tested in CI

Test Workflow What It Validates
devtools::check() R-CMD-check.yml Package loads, tests pass, docs build, CRAN-level checks
targets::tar_validate() R-CMD-check.yml Pipeline DAG is valid
nix-build package.nix R-CMD-check.yml Nix derivation builds, package installs via Nix
remotes::install_github() R-CMD-check.yml (github-install-test job) Non-Nix users can install from GitHub
tar_make() + vignettes data-update.yml Pipeline runs end-to-end, vignettes render

CI loads irishbuoys from local source checkout (not from cachix). extraPullNames: johngavin provides binary R dependencies (dplyr, targets, etc.), not the irishbuoys package itself.

Nix Installer

All workflows use DeterminateSystems/nix-installer-action@main for better logging and diagnostics than cachix/install-nix-action.

Explicit nix-build Step

All workflows include an explicit nix-build step before nix-shell:

- name: Build development environment
  run: nix-build default.nix -A shell --no-out-link

This gives clearer error messages if the environment fails to build (separate from the actual command failure).

Failure Artifacts

All workflows upload artifacts on failure for post-mortem debugging:

- name: Upload check results on failure
  if: failure()
  uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
  with:
    name: failure-results
    path: check/

Static Data API (MANDATORY)

Every project with derived data MUST expose it as static JSON on GitHub Pages.

  • Pattern: R/tar_plans/plan_api.R -> docs/api/v1/*.json -> weekly CI commits
  • Endpoints: index, stations/entities, stats, key derived datasets, data-dictionary
  • generate_api_latest(n) parameterised for N most recent observations
  • Vignette api-usage.qmd documents all endpoints with curl/R/Python examples
  • See static-api-deployment skill for full implementation pattern

Table Display in Vignettes

  • All tables MUST use DT::datatable() (NEVER knitr::kable())
  • DT::datatable() provides sorting, filtering, search, pagination
  • Every DT::datatable() MUST have caption=

Data in Package (R-exts 1.1.6 Compliance)

See data-in-packages rule for full requirements.

Known issues in irishbuoys: - inst/extdata/irish_buoys.duckdb (58 MB) ships with every install. Problem: connect_duckdb() defaults to db_path = "inst/extdata/irish_buoys.duckdb", so the 58 MB database is inside the installed package. Every install.packages() or remotes::install_github() downloads it. Remedy (future): Change the default db_path to rappdirs::user_cache_dir("irishbuoys") (e.g. ~/Library/Caches/irishbuoys/irish_buoys.duckdb on macOS). On first call, connect_duckdb() would download the database from a release asset or static URL and cache it locally. Subsequent calls reuse the cached file. The database would then be removed from inst/extdata/ entirely. - inst/extdata/ctx/*.ctx.yaml are dev-only LLM context files, not runtime data. Status: Excluded from package builds via .Rbuildignore. plan_pkgctx.R still writes here for local development use, but the files never ship with the installed package. Dependency contexts should migrate to the centralised llmcontent package. - Snapshot tests use monotonic assertions for growing data (counts, ranges) and expect_snapshot() only for stable properties (schema, earliest dates).

Centralised Package Context (llmcontent)

.ctx.yaml files for standard R packages (dplyr, targets, ggplot2, etc.) are stored centrally in the llmcontent package, NOT duplicated per project.

  • Central repo: /Users/johngavin/docs_gh/proj/data/llm/content/
  • External packages: inst/ctx/external/<pkg>.ctx.yaml (CRAN/Bioc)
  • Local projects: inst/ctx/local/<pkg>.ctx.yaml (symlinks to source repos)
  • Workflow: llmcontent::sync_project(".") reads DESCRIPTION, calls ensure_context() for each dependency, generates/updates .ctx.yaml
  • Per-project: Only self-context (e.g. irishbuoys.ctx.yaml) lives in each project at inst/extdata/ctx/, excluded from build via .Rbuildignore. plan_pkgctx.R generates self-context ONLY — no dependency targets.
  • NEVER generate dependency contexts per-project. They come from llmcontent.
  • See: llm-package-context skill for pkgctx commands and CI workflows
